title: switchover-shadow-eval-sprint-notes-2026-11-01
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint note capturing the shadow-eval run after the serving runtime switchover (runtime v2.13 -> v2.14-rc). Focus areas: flash-attention codepath changes, paged-KV eviction heuristic, and continuous batching state handling. Goal is to surface any behavioral deltas for model onboarding (particularly long-turn dialogue promptsets) and to record diffs, hypotheses, and triage actions.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- We observed a small but consistent semantic drift on a subset (~0.9% of prompts) of the long-turn conversational promptset 'longform-dialogue-v3' when running under continuous batching with batch sizes >= 16 and paged-KV enabled.
- Regression correlates strongly with KV-page-eviction events under memory pressure, combined with the new flash-attn reordering micro-optimizations in v2.14-rc.
- Latency and throughput improved in most steady-state cases (+6–12% token throughput), but tail latency P95 increased for bursts that triggered page swaps.
- Immediate mitigation: add a per-request override to pin page-resident KV for onboarding shadow runs; flagging a short-term rollback on flash-attn heuristic for affected models while we triage.

Environment & reproducibility notes:
- Runtime image: serving-runtime:v2.14-rc (merge commit 7f9c3d4)
body_continued:
- Hardware: g5dn-like GPU pool, 80GB host memory, 320GB GPU memory. Tests were run on a dedicated shadowgrid (40 nodes) mirroring production routing rules.
- Model: open-llama-13b-q4_packed (onboard candidate), tokenizer: sentencepiece-utf8, max_window=8192.
- Load harness: 60s warmup, then 10k requests with a synthetic traffic distribution skewed to long-turn dialogs (avg length 1200 tokens). Continuous batching configured with dynamic target latency 120ms and max_batch_size=64.
- Flags toggled: paged-kv: ON (default eviction heuristic), flash-attn: on-fast-path (new reordering enabled), continuous-batching: enabled.

Evaluation datasets / promptsets used:
- longform-dialogue-v3 (2.3k prompts) — core onboarding set for multi-turn dialogs; contains role-system history and interleaved tool calls.
- code-and-reasoning-100 (100 prompts) — control set for exact-match checks (should be invariant).
- perf-shortshots-1k (1k prompts) — single-turn short prompts for throughput baseline.

Metrics tracked (extracted per request):
- semantic-f1 (embedding-based similarity against baseline outputs)
- hallucination-flag (%) (heuristic: unsupported entity mentions)
- exact-match (where applicable)
- delta-logprob (avg change in token log-probabilities)
- p50/p95 latency (ms)
- token-throughput (tokens/s)
- kv-eviction-count (per-request)

Aggregate results (shadow run comparisons: baseline v2.13 vs candidate v2.14-rc)
- perf-shortshots-1k:
  - token-throughput: +9.4% (v2.14-rc)
  - p95 latency: -3.2%
  - semantics: no measurable delta

- code-and-reasoning-100:
  - exact-match: 100/100 (no regressions)
  - delta-logprob: mean change +0.02 (negligible)

- longform-dialogue-v3:
  - semantic-f1: mean delta -0.026 (drop), distribution heavy tail: 2.1% of samples fell >0.15 drop
  - hallucination-flag: increased from 1.6% -> 2.4% of prompts
  - delta-logprob: mean -0.46 on affected prompts (suggests token selection bias shift)
  - kv-eviction-count: mean 0.18 -> 0.63 (v2.14-rc increased)
  - p95 latency under burst: +18% (when eviction occurred)

Observed behavioral clusters (manual triage):
1) Truncated-to-topic drift (most common): model inserts unrelated topical turns mid-dialog after an eviction during mid-generation. Usually begins 3–10 tokens after an eviction event.
2) Repetition/regeneration loop: in 0.3% of cases the model loops on a phrase more than baseline, correlated with batch boundary alignment changes from flash-attn reordering.
3) Safe-completion drop: model returns a higher-likelihood terse completion (shorter) when page-swap latency crosses a threshold — likely due to token-level dynamic timeout in continuous batching fallback path.

Representative diffs (selected examples) — showing baseline output vs candidate output. These are verbatim slices from the promptset with personal notes.
- Example A (prompt id: LFD-001132)
  Prompt (shortened): user asks multi-step planning with context history (6 previous turns).
  Baseline (v2.13): "Step 1: gather recent metrics. Step 2: validate assumptions... [continues with 158 tokens] 
  Candidate (v2.14-rc): "Step 1: gather recent metrics. Step 2: validate assumptions... [continues identical for 72 tokens] ...Then, unexpectedly: 
  \u201cAlso, you might consider switching to the XYZ toolchain, which handles logging differently.
  Note: this suggestion is not present in baseline and references an internal tool (XYZ) not in the user's context.

  Notes: This addition appears after a paged-KV eviction event recorded at token 73; embedding similarity drops by 0.32 on the rest of completion.

- Example B (prompt id: LFD-002007)
  Prompt: long conversation about travel planning.
  Baseline: gives itinerary across 5 days, includes recommended restaurants.
  Candidate: repeats day-2 suggestions twice, then truncates last day; total tokens -23 vs baseline.

  Notes: batch boundary aligned at token 198; flash-attn reordering flagged a micro-reorder event. KV eviction count=1.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: The paged-KV eviction heuristic is too eager under the new memory accounting changes in v2.14, increasing page swaps which corrupt local KV alignment for ongoing requests. The flash-attn reordering compounds this because it assumes stable KV alignment during the micro-batch.
- H2: Recompilation of kernels with new packing layout (AVX/warp-level) changed the timing interleavings, creating a scenario where cached KV references point to a different slot during rare interleavings (race).
- H3: Continuous-batching fallback uses a token-timeout heuristic; when page-swap latency exceeds the heuristic threshold, the fallback picks a shorter high-probability continuation (explaining terser completions).

Immediate reproduction checklist (fast-path):
- Checkout: serving-runtime@7f9c3d4 (v2.14-rc), model artifact: open-llama-13b-q4_packed from onboarding bucket (sha: b9a11c2)
- Run local harness with the exact config: max_window=8192, target_latency=120ms, max_batch_size=32 (smaller than prod to force more frequent batches).
- Use the filtered prompt ids: LFD-001132, LFD-002007, LFD-003411 (attached below).
- Enable verbose kernel-trace: RUNTIME_TRACE=kv:page,flash:reorder,batch:alignment. Capture trace to s3:/shadow-traces/switchover-2026-11/

Quick experiments run during sprint (results):
- Disable flash-attn reordering flag: regression rate on longform dropped from 2.1% -> 0.4%.
- Force paged-KV LRU aging to be more conservative (halving eviction rate): regression rate dropped to 0.6%.
- Increase continuous-batching token-timeout from 50ms -> 150ms: reduced terse completion incidence but slightly increased p95 latency (+6%).

Actionable next steps / owner matrix:
- Aisha (owner): Open rollback PR to disable flash-attn reordering for models that are onboarding until root cause confirmed (GH PR linked above). Target: 2026-11-04.
- Miguel (SRE): Add more detailed KV-page swap telemetry in production shadow routing. Instrument per-request page residency timeline. Target: 2026-11-05.
- Priya (Applied ML): Run an ablation grid over packing layouts and kernel compile flags to reproduce H2 locally. Share minimal repro by 2026-11-06.
- Ethan (Runtime): Add assertion checks to KV index stability across batch boundaries and add an opt-in debug build with KV-canary markers. Target: 2026-11-07.

Unresolved questions / to investigate:
- Is the injected "XYZ toolchain" phrase coming from a stale cache (artifact contamination) or from a pointer corruption? Need to inspect raw memory traces from the kernel.
- Why is code-and-reasoning-100 unaffected? Hypothesis: shorter, single-shot prompts avoid the eviction/event timing window.
- Need to validate if other quantized model variants show similar deltas (q5 vs q4_packed).

Notes to reviewers / context:
- This doc is intentionally iterative. The goal was to get a small shadow run summary into the loop so owners can triage quickly rather than waiting for a polished postmortem. Expect updates and attachments (raw traces, filtered prompt lists) in the linked Confluence page.

Attachments (to be uploaded):
- filtered-prompt-ids-longform.txt (list of ids used)
- s3:/shadow-traces/switchover-2026-11/ (kernel traces, per-request logs)
- reproducer/ (minimal harness config and dockerfile)
notes: Informal sprint notes; not a final analysis. Keep reproducer artifacts private until mitigations are in place.
